subsystem: Source media (key: media) — own-dashboard #114: article/Instagram picture collection, marketing-media bucket, read model for briefs, generation and the editor
summary: The media step is small, well-tested (6 files, 56 tests, 2.5 s) and strict: one page read per selected feed candidate (og:image/twitter:image, the feed image, body figures from a 12-entry publisher-host allowlist), Instagram CDN URLs fetched the same night, bytes stored once per owner under sha256 in the private marketing-media bucket with credit, pHash, EXIF-corrected dimensions, and a 30-day purge of unreferenced bytes in the daily tick. The capability flags are derived at read time from two constants (short side >= 900 full-bleed, width >= 600 inset), so no migration is needed to change them. The weak spots are supply and understanding, not plumbing: with feeds only, no event can get a full-bleed cover (typical og:image 1200x630 fails 900 px and would need a 2.14x upscale against the studio's 1.5x cap), openai.com 403s the page read and leaves those events pictureless, nothing looks at pixels (no vision or text-slide check), alt/figcaption/og:image:alt are discarded so the model picks pictures blind, off-host pictures are dropped silently, there is no owner upload or licensed fallback, Apify carousels (the only 1080x1350-native supply) are switched off, and docs/dneskai-source-media.md:28-29 still says nothing in the app calls these functions.

facts.fact: pHash is the classic 32x32 grey DCT, 8x8 low frequencies, 64 bits as 16 hex digits; the database marks a new asset a duplicate of the nearest canonical within Hamming distance <= 6 that is at least as large (groups flat, never chained); the brief repeat check uses <= 3 bits.

findings.title: Social-card pictures can never give a full-bleed cover: og:image 1200x630 fails the 900 px gate and would need 2.14x against the studio 1.5x cap
findings.claim: With Apify off, the only pictures are publisher og:images (1200x630, 1024x683) and body figures. The 900 px short-side rule (equivalent to the studio's 1.5x upscale cap on a 1350 px canvas) makes every social card inset-only, so rules.firstSlide can never be cover-photo and a single post can never be the photo variant; 0 of the 3 pictures stored on night 1 qualify by the sizes the brief reports. Lowering the threshold alone cannot help because the studio refuses > 1.5x; a new composition is needed. [Verifier: body figures can qualify; night 1 stored one 1920x1080 Anthropic figure that is full-bleed capable, so 1 of 3, not 0 of 3.]

impact.ownerDecision: Accept a new photo composition (band) in the DNESKAi kit; it changes the look and crosses quorum/studio or waits for consolidation.
impact.reason: Most events carry only a social card, so a band layout is the realistic way to get a picture on the cover; the claim is overstated, the need is real.

findings.recommendation: Add one duotone-free 'band' composition to the photo kit (quorum/studio, then re-vendor): the picture spans the full 1080 px width at <= 1.5x upscale, cropped to a band of up to 945 px for 1200x630 (70 % of the canvas) or 1024 px for 1024x683, with the headline on the remaining paper strip; and a 'whole picture' variant at 0.9x (1080x567 band) for charts. Add a third flag bandCapable = width >= 720 (1080/1.5) in dneskaiMediaCapabilities and offer it to the model as the first-slide rule when nothing is fullBleedCapable. truth.evidence: Code confirmed: dneskai-media-plan.ts:30,34 (min side >= 900), dneskai-generation.ts:229-230 (firstSlide cover-photo only when a fullBleedCapable picture is offered), quorum studio dneskai-slide.ts:44 (MAX_UPSCALE = 1350/900) and :389. But "feed pictures can never give a full-bleed cover" and "0 of 3 qualify" are wrong: Supabase SELECT 22 Oct 2026 on marketing_media_assets shows 3 assets, and the anthropic-news article-figure is 1920x1080 (full-bleed capable). Body figures can qualify; og:images cannot.

findings.impactStatement: Every feed-sourced post opens with a framed figure or a typographic statement, never an edge-to-edge photo: the least scroll-stopping first slide the kit has. The owner cannot fix it in the editor (the render refuses). Quality cost on every post until Apify is on.

findings.title: Nothing looks at the pixels: no vision or text-slide check before a picture is offered
findings.claim: The collector derives sha256, format, size and pHash only; the model is told it cannot see pictures and must never describe them; the editor shows a 128 px thumbnail. A designed text slide from an Instagram carousel, a publisher logo card, a watermarked or blurry image or a picture unrelated to the headline passes every gate. Quorum's hero ladder has a vision gate with nine vetoes (wrong-subject, recognisable-face, logo-or-watermark, embedded-text, low-quality, ...); OwnDashboard has none.

impact.ownerDecision: Approve per-asset vision spend (Haiku-class call, cents per post) or keep only the free sharp-statistics layer.

findings.recommendation: Two layers. (1) Free, in inspectDneskaiImage: sharp stats per asset (entropy, edge density, colour-count flatness, aspect) into a `quality` jsonb column and read-model fields `textSlideLikely`, `lowDetail`; briefs drop textSlideLikely from the usable count, the tray shows a badge. (2) Optional, owner-approved spend: one Haiku-class vision call per offered asset (~12 per post, well under a cent) answering 'does this picture show the subject of this headline? any text/watermark/face?' with LangSmith receiving codes only; failures descend to the typographic slide, never to a generated image. Port the veto vocabulary from quorum/orchestrator/src/images/vision-gate.ts rather than inventing a new one.

findings.impactStatement: The owner is the only quality gate and sees thumbnails: a wrong or text-covered picture reaches review, costs an edit-and-re-render cycle (minutes per post) or ships. Once Apify carousels are on (mostly designed slides, not photographs) this becomes the main failure mode.

findings.impactStatement: Thin evidence forces single-image, low-information posts and invites the model to pad; richer primary text is the single biggest lever for truthful 4-7 slide carousels at zero extra network cost (the bytes are already downloaded).
